newsitem.title: PERU: Another ancient tomb found at Sipan site in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Another ancient tomb found at Sipan site in Peru.

text.p: Archaeologists have discovered the tomb of an ancient military officer bedecked in silver and gold only steps away from the mausoleum of the famous Lord of Sipan in northern Peru, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The tomb, dating from about the year 50 A.D., has thrown light on the ancient Moche society because it shows an important military figure buried near governors and priests, said the report in the Lima newspaper El Comercio.
The grave lies in the Huaca Rajada burial mound near the northern Peruvian city of Chiclayo, said El Comercio.

The same mound held the tomb of the Lord of Sipan, an ancient personality whose tomb contained tonnes of dazzling gold, silver and turquoise objects excavated in the early 1990s and shown in a hit museum show in 1995 in New York.
The Sipan discovery was the subject of a National Geographic cover story and hailed as one of the great archaeological discoveries of the late 20th century.
The new discovery includes silver necklaces, gold nose plates, elaborate necklaces made from seashells, sceptres and other objects similar to those found in the Lord of Sipan tomb, said El Comercio.

"This confirms that in the royal mausoleum, not only governors, priests and other personalities were buried but also the military class, which was one of the powers that governed the Moche kingdom," El Comercio quoted Peruvian archaeologist Luis Chero Zurita as saying.
The objects found alongside the anonymous soldier, who stood about 5 feet (1.6 metres) tall, are in good condition and include various crowns, belts and ceramics, said the report.
